concept.name: Three outside up
concept.definition: A three-candlestick bullish reversal pattern introduced by Gregory Morris as a confirmed bullish engulfing: a black body in a downtrend is engulfed by a larger white body (the engulfing), and then a third white candle closes above the second candle's close. The third candle's higher close confirms the engulfing signal.
concept.intuition: Buyers first swallow the prior down candle whole, then prove it was no fluke by closing higher again the very next session.
concept.mechanics: From OHLC data: candle 1 is a black body; candle 2 is a long white body engulfing body 1 (O2 <= C1, C2 >= O1); candle 3 is a white candle closing above C2. Shadows are disregarded. Further confirmation may be sought in a break of nearby resistance or a trendline.
concept.formula: Three outside up when C1 < O1, O2 <= C1, C2 >= O1, C2 > O2, and C3 > C2 (with candle 3 white).
concept.failure_modes: Despite the extra confirmation candle, the pattern still fails regularly in persistent downtrends; published S&P 500 scan statistics show a substantial share of false signals. Late entry after the third candle can leave a poor risk-reward location.
concept.misconceptions: It is not a synonym for bullish engulfing; it is the engulfing plus a confirming third candle. It is also a modern Morris construction rather than a classical Japanese pattern.
concept.example: In a downtrend, a stock prints a black candle (45.00 to 43.50), a long white candle engulfing it (43.20 to 45.50), then a third white candle closing at 46.10. The three outside up is read as a confirmed bullish reversal.
